body.statement: Theorem 5. For fixed \(H\), \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\), and \(\eta\in(0,1-\alpha)\), \[\sqrt{1-\alpha-\eta}\,L_H(V^{\mathrm{quad}}_r)^{1/4}\le r^*_{\alpha,\eta}(H,r)\le\{\alpha^{-1/2}+\eta^{-1/2}\}^{1/2}(V^{\mathrm{quad}}_r)^{1/4}.\] Thus \(r^*_{\alpha,\eta}(H,r)\asymp r^{-1/4}\). The identity \(V^{\mathrm{quad}}_r=v_H/(rh^2)\), its attainment, the computable lower constant \(L_H\), exact worst-null calibration, and the all-test converse form a graph-specific repeated-motif testing frontier. As a sanity reduction, when every vertex has degree two, the three attainable-support moment equations force \(\mathcal W_H=\{w^G\}\), so the optimized quadratic statistic coincides with the fixed Section 4 and Appendix B weight of GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026; there is no motifwise variance improvement over that fixed weight in this degree-two case.
body.justification: The theorem makes optimized conditional variance both sufficient and necessary.
body.gap: GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026 arXiv version 2 Section 4 and Appendix B construct the quadratic statistic, Proposition 4.1 gives its \(d_{\max}^5/n\) MSE envelope, and Lemmas S3--S4 supply the variance ingredients; they do not identify the attained repeated-motif conditional-variance constant, exact composite-null calibration, or its necessity for testing. Tiwari--Basu leave theoretical power open.
body.consumer: A platform can report a graph-specific detection floor before running the experiment.
